name: Erythromelalgia

criteria.description: Burning pain in extremities (typically feet, sometimes hands)
Erythema (redness) of affected areas during episodes
Increased temperature of affected skin during episodes
Symptoms triggered or exacerbated by heat or exercise
Symptoms relieved by cooling (immersion in cold water, cold packs)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical triad of intermittent burning pain, erythema, and warmth of the extremities, typically triggered by heat and relieved by cooling. Primary vs secondary forms must be distinguished.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Primary (idiopathic or genetic) vs secondary (myeloproliferative disorders, especially polycythemia vera and essential thrombocythemia; neuropathies; medications). SCN9A mutations cause inherited form.

searchTerms: loss of sensation in hands and feet
no response when tapping ankle tendon

laboratory: CBC with differential: evaluate for myeloproliferative disorders (elevated platelets, RBC, WBC)
JAK2 V617F mutation testing if myeloproliferative disorder suspected
Routine labs typically normal in primary erythromelalgia
imaging: Infrared thermography may demonstrate temperature elevation during episodes
genetic: SCN9A gene mutations (Nav1.7 sodium channel): autosomal dominant inherited erythromelalgia
other: Skin biopsy: may show reduced intraepidermal nerve fiber density
Provocative testing: warming the extremity reproduces symptoms
Aspirin challenge: dramatic response to aspirin suggests secondary (myeloproliferative) form
Bone marrow biopsy if myeloproliferative disorder suspected

distinguishingFeatures: Raynaud is triggered by cold, not heat
Raynaud causes pallor/cyanosis rather than erythema/warmth
Neuropathy pain is constant rather than episodic
Cellulitis has progressive rather than episodic course
Cellulitis does not improve with cooling

redFlags: New-onset erythromelalgia in adults (screen for myeloproliferative neoplasms)
Elevated platelet count or polycythemia (consider essential thrombocythemia or PV)
Tissue damage from excessive cooling behaviors
Severe refractory pain unresponsive to treatment
references: Davis MD, et al. Erythromelalgia: clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment. Mayo Clin Proc. 2000;75(6):587-601.
Dib-Hajj SD, et al. Gain-of-function mutation in Nav1.7 in familial erythromelalgia induces bursting of sensory neurons. Brain. 2005;128(Pt 8):1847-1854.
Mann N, et al. Erythromelalgia: a practical approach. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019;81(5):1157-1167.
